blocks.content: While Continental Drift posited that continents plowed through the ocean floor, Plate Tectonic Theory proved that continents and ocean floors move together as lithospheric plates over the asthenosphere.

rows: Thermal convection currents in the mantle
Jigsaw fit, fossils, tillite, rocks across oceans

items: Wegener cited jigsaw fit of coastlines, matching fossil distributions (Mesosaurus, Glossopteris), and tillite glacial deposits as primary evidence for Continental Drift.
Mid-Oceanic Ridges are constructive/divergent boundaries where seafloor spreading creates new oceanic crust.
The Circum-Pacific 'Ring of Fire' is formed along convergent plate boundaries where subduction leads to intense volcanic and seismic activity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Alfred Wegener proposed the Continental Drift Theory in 1912, hypothesizing that all landmasses were once part of a supercontinent named Pangea surrounded by Panthalassa.
Plate Tectonic Theory, formulated in the 1960s, explains that the Earth's lithosphere is divided into major and minor plates floating on the semi-fluid asthenosphere.
Continental Drift attributed movement to gravitational/tidal forces, which was rejected; Plate Tectonics successfully identified thermal convection currents in the mantle as the true driving force.
Tectonic plate interactions occur along three main types of boundaries: Divergent (constructive), Convergent (destructive), and Transform (conservative).
